content.text: •pain/discomfort in LUQ, left shoulder pain, &/or early satiety
•LUQ, left chest wall, or left shoulder pain that is worse w/ inspiration
•may be associated w/ shortness of breath and exertional symptoms
•acute-onset, persistent upper abdominal pain radiating to the back
•epigastric pain or discomfort is the most prominent symptom
•abdominal discomfort/pain, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, and hematemesis
•postprandial fullness, early satiation, epigastric pain, or burning
•N/V, abdominal pain, early satiety, postprandial fullness, and bloating
•intense, dull discomfort located in the RUQ or epigastrium
•generally lasts at least 30 minutes, plateauing within one hour
•prolonged (>4 to 6 hours) RUQ or epigastric pain, fever
•RUQ pain with fatigue, malaise, N/V, & anorexia
•may also have jaundice, dark urine, and light-colored stools
•RUQ pain with a pleuritic component, pain is sometimes referred to the right shoulder
•symptoms include fever, abdominal pain, abdominal distention (from ascites), lower extremity edema, jaundice, gastrointestinal bleeding, &/or hepatic encephalopathy
•periumbilical pain initially that radiates to the RLQ
•LLQ pain usually constant & present for several days prior to presentation
•pain MC symptom, varies from mild to severe
•generally flank pain, but may have back or abdominal pain
•associated w/ dysuria, frequency, urgency, hematuria, fever, chills, flank pain, & CVA
•present w/ lower abdominal pain and discomfort; inability to urinate
•diarrhea as the predominant symptom, but may also have associated abdominal pain, which may be severe
